A-female:
Create one professional two-panel landscape character design plate for Veles, original grounded preindustrial dark-fantasy action RPG. Two panels touch at a straight vertical division exactly at 40% width. No text, borders, interface, logos, diagrams or insets. LEFT 40%: single head-to-toe front three-quarter character study at 85% of panel height, feet visible, against warm plain light grey, enough clean margin around all tools, softly lit face and readable gesture. RIGHT 60%: a single authentic widescreen THIRD-PERSON GAMEPLAY frame, full figure seen directly FROM BEHIND, head and both boots visible, mid-step away from viewer on a wet-limestone causeway in Veles. Trailing camera at shoulder height, character near lower center-left of the panel, head at about 41% viewport height and boots at 92%, natural 55 degree horizontal field of view, no foreground objects obscuring player. Character geometry and equipped tools must agree between the two views. The landscape is exactly this: a low ruined one-arch stone bridge straight ahead, timber riverside workshop with red-brown roof on left, silver river and two pale birches on right, misted hills; soft grey morning, broken gold light from upper left. Emphasize the route and silhouette through directional light and value grouping. Draw game-quality naturalistic PBR surfaces, lyrical atmospheric depth and serious human proportions. Both reference mosaics jointly inform silhouette separation and environmental composition; do not reproduce IP, individual characters, casual or cute aesthetics, machinery, firearms, modern gear, mounts or sci-fi motifs. This is about a memorable playable craftsperson with a visually logical load, not a generic medieval adventurer.
A | BRIDGE MEASURING-INSTRUMENT MAKER. A needle-like vertical silhouette: conspicuously tall and wiry, long shins and long neck, erect watchful posture, narrow shoulders, very slim fitted calf-length indigo work coat with two straight side slits and linen collar, elongated silhouette down to slim boots. A single folded, long straight surveyor's staff with an open rectangular brass sight at its tip carried vertically beside the body, slightly above head height, like a giant scale rule with visible graduation marks, unmistakably an instrument. Small pear-shaped plumb bob on a short cord at hip. Empty back, elegant vertical lines, lucid features. Precision craft.
Adult woman, about 48, long bony face, grey-flecked black hair braided in a tight vertical knot, focused hooded eyes.
